title: Compare answers, catch a planted error
statement: Give guided practice that compares and corrects: students pick the better of two responses and say why, or stop a model answer at a planted error and fix it.
example: A replication with 390 students confirmed a delayed-test advantage for erroneous examples.
detail: The Grade 9 lesson design specification has two such modes of guided practice: comparative judgement, where students see two responses side by side, pick the one that better answers the learning question and explain why, and an intercept mode, where a model answer writes itself out until the student stops it at the error, highlights the mistake and corrects it; it proposes recording each planted error so that errors are designed on purpose, not improvised (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0204-g9-year-9-ela-lesson-design-specification.qmd`). Its reading list grounds the first in adaptive comparative judgement (Pollitt 2012) and the second in studies of erroneous examples, whose larger follow-up with 390 students confirmed their delayed-test advantage (McLaren, Adams & Mayer 2015) (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0251-g9-prep-pack-index-manifests-leadership-playbook.qmd`).
against: The erroneous-examples studies taught decimals with a web-based tutoring system, not writing about a text (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0251-g9-prep-pack-index-manifests-leadership-playbook.qmd`), and the specification notes that in the research 'faded examples' usually means steps removed for the learner to complete, so its intercept mode is closer to erroneous examples (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0204-g9-year-9-ela-lesson-design-specification.qmd`).
